chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the catch of fish, even if not named (specifically), and he said: There is no harm. And I asked him about the catch of the Magians (Zoroastrians), 'Do I eat the fish?' He said: I would not eat it until I look at it.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat fish caught by Zoroastrians according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the general permissibility of fish where the catcher's name is unspecified and the specific caution required for fish caught by Zoroastrians (Magians), mandating visual inspection to ensure purity. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) versus *ihtiyat* (precaution) when dealing with *Ahl al- Kitab* whose meat consumption is debated, emphasizing that visual confirmation of the catch's nature is necessary to validate its halal status. The requirement to 'look at it' underscores the importance of verifying the physical state of the food source when the catcher's religious status introduces potential impurity (*najasah*) or doubt.
